summary: Add customer_note column, backfill from note, create a PostgreSQL BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that synchronizes note and customer_note on every write from either version, deploy the new version with a state-only migration, retire the old version, and drop the note column. The trigger ensures both columns always hold identical values, preventing the cross-version divergence that caused the previous plan's 15 check failures.
write_consistency: A database trigger on account_user keeps note and customer_note synchronized: on INSERT or UPDATE, if one column is written by a version, the other column is set to the same value. This guarantees that the GraphQL field note always returns the most recently written value regardless of which version performed the write.
revision_notes: Root cause: the previous plans performed only a one-time backfill (UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note) but had no mechanism to keep note and customer_note synchronized during concurrent traffic from both versions. The old version wrote to column note, the new version wrote to column customer_note, causing the columns to diverge. The runner's cross-version checks (old_write_new_read, new_write_old_read, alternating writes, etc.) all failed because reads from the expected column returned stale seed values instead of the most recently written note. This plan adds a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that copies the written value to the other column, maintaining the invariant note = customer_note throughout the zero-downtime overlap.

stages.description: Add customer_note column and backfill its values from note so both columns start equal.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;

stages.description: Create a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that keeps note and customer_note in sync on every write from either version.
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN IF NEW.note IS NOT NULL AND NEW.customer_note IS NULL THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; ELSIF NEW.customer_note IS NOT NULL AND NEW.note IS NULL THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; ELSIF NEW.note IS NOT NULL AND NEW.customer_note IS NOT NULL THEN IF NEW.note != NEW.customer_customer_note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; END IF; ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; ELSIF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER note_customer_sync_trig BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Retire the old version; after this point only the new version serves traffic.
Drop the old note column; customer_note now the sole note column.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
